case_name: Shivnarayan Laxminarayan Joshi and Others v State of Maharashtra and another
respondent:
State of Maharashtra and another
Supreme Court of India

10 October 1979
Cr.As. Nos. 179 of 1972 (Along with Cr.A. No. 178 of 1972) and 251 and 252 of 1973.
The Judgment was delivered by: FAZAL ALI, J.
1. These appeals by special leave are directed against the judgment of the Bombay High Court by which the conviction and sentence of the appellants under Section 120-B, 477-A and 409 of the Indian Penal Code were upheld or modified to some extent. So far as appellant 1 is concerned, who was also accused 1 at the trial, his appeal is limited to the question of sentence as also the nature of the offence. The special leave granted to A-24 is open. Since all these appeals were decided by the High Court by one judgment we also propose to dispose of the appeals by one common judgment. The facts of the case have been detailed in the judgment of the courts below and it is not necessary for us to repeat the same over and over again.

facts: These appeals by special leave are directed against the judgment of the Bombay High Court by which the conviction and sentence of the appellants under Section 120-B, 477-A and 409 of the Indian Penal Code were upheld or modified to some extent.
The facts of the case have been detailed in the judgment of the courts below and it is not necessary for us to repeat the same over and over again.
issues: Whether the findings of facts are vitiated by a grave error of law or by an error which leads to serious and substantial miscarriage of justice.
Whether the substitution of one chose action for another will amount to a breach of trust or conversion to his own use by the accused.
petitioner_arguments: The first contention raised by Mr. Chitale must be overruled.
Secondly, it was contended that substitution of one chose action for another will not amount to a breach of trust or conversion to his own use by the accused.
It was also urged that there is no evidence or finding that the appellant 1 had dominion over the properties misappropriated.
respondent_arguments: The High Court has, however, found that so far as accused 2, 3 and 4 were concerned they were original conspirators who had assisted and abetted appellant 1 in his attempt to misappropriate the amount.
The High Court has dealt with these aspects at great length and we agree with the findings arrived at by the High Court on this aspect also.
court_reasoning: It is well settled that this Court in special leave will not interfere with concurrent findings of facts unless the findings are vitiated by a grave error of law or by an error which leads to serious and substantial miscarriage of justice.

After a perusal of the record and judgment of the High Court we find ourselves in complete agreement with the view taken by the High Court and unable to find any special circumstances which require our interference with the order passed by the High Court.
holding: The appeal of appellant 1 is dismissed.
We do not see any reason to reduce the sentences of any of these appellants.
If these appellants are not keeping good health the Jail Superintendent would naturally take care of them and get them properly treated in the Jail Hospital
